data.title: BT
data.headline: Turning frontline managers into catalysts for culture change.
data.introduction: Partnering with BT to equip 2,200 frontline managers across more than 20 countries to lead people, not simply manage performance, and help translate a changing culture into everyday behaviour.
data.challenge: BT was undergoing significant cultural change. Yet for many frontline managers, success had historically centred on business performance, operational delivery and KPIs. Pioneers represented an important shift: managers were now being asked to take genuine ownership for people, culture and performance together. The challenge was to make that transition practical and relevant across 2,200 managers, multiple businesses and more than 20 countries, without turning leadership into theory.
data.approach: CorporateDNA designed Pioneers, a four-part global development journey built around short, practical learning modules and the everyday realities of frontline management. Rather than teaching leadership as an abstract competency, managers worked on real conversations, real people challenges and real business scenarios, repeatedly practising new behaviours between modules and bringing their learning back into the workplace. The experience strengthened the fundamentals of highly effective management: setting expectations, coaching performance, giving feedback, navigating difficult conversations, creating accountability and building ownership within teams.
data.outcome: Pioneers helped move frontline management from compliance and instruction towards greater ownership, challenge and growth mindset. Managers became more confident addressing people issues alongside operational priorities and more accountable for creating the conditions in which their teams could perform. Across the programme, engagement measures were 73 to 81% higher*, while the scale of the intervention helped establish a shared leadership language across countries and organisational boundaries.
data.bannerStatement: Build managers who turn strategy into performance through people.
data.challengeHeadline: From managing KPIs to leading people.
data.approachHeadline: Building leadership into the flow of work.
data.outcomeHeadline: Changing culture through the layer that makes it real.
data.closingThought: Culture doesn’t cascade. It travels through people. Pioneers strengthened the layer where strategy, leadership and employee experience meet every day.
data.additionalContent:
Wider transformation story:
The programme also contributed to BT’s broader cultural evolution, from a more subservient, compliance-led environment towards one characterised by growth, constructive challenge and collective ownership. Critically, the work connected different organisational layers: senior leaders setting direction, middle leaders translating it, and frontline managers making it real through thousands of everyday decisions and conversations.

Impact: 85% talent retention (high potential programme); 45% higher promotion rate (same programme); 88% programme impact (same programme). Scale: 60 high potential leaders, from board coaching.

data.title: DP World
data.quote:
The programme helped me connect who I am as a leader to how I show up every day. It's changed how I lead conversations, build trust, and inspire my teams."
North Carolina participant
data.challenge: As DP World expanded rapidly across continents, it faced a pivotal challenge: unifying language, mindsets and behaviours across a diverse global workforce. With varying levels of maturity and different cultural contexts across more than 80 ports and terminals worldwide, there was a pressing need to define a single  standard, 'The DP World Way', that connects identity, purpose and performance. Priorities included building a common global vocabulary, equipping first-time and mid-level managers to lead with confidence and clarity, and embedding the DP World Way as a living culture rather than a corporate statement.
data.approach: We designed and piloted a global first time manager programme reaching more than 120 mid-level managers across four pilot regions: the Middle East, Africa, Asia and the Americas. The facilitator model was built alongside DP World's internal HR and learning partners from the outset, so the programme could scale into a global rollout rather than remain a one-off intervention.
data.outcome: A unified first time manager culture is now established across the pilot regions, driving consistency, accountability and high trust. Managers demonstrated measurable behavioural change, including improved clarity in decision-making, stronger collaboration and better coaching conversations, translating into sharper execution as teams, terminals and time zones aligned around a common way of leading peers and teams. Consistency is now embedded across DP World's multi-national environments and functions, giving the organisation cultural continuity as it continues to scale.
data.bannerStatement: Build managers who turn strategy into performance through people.

data.title: Dyson
data.headline: Removing the organisational friction that slows innovation.
data.introduction: Partnering with Dyson’s Group CEO, Executive Committee and Research, Design and Development leadership to strengthen enterprise leadership, remove bottlenecks and create greater trust, flow and ownership across the innovation system.
data.challenge: Dyson’s Executive Committee brought together leaders accountable for major global functions and markets. The opportunity was to help them become more than a collection of highly capable functional leaders: a highly effective enterprise team, able to look beyond individual portfolios, navigate competing priorities and collectively lead Dyson as a whole. That same challenge of interdependence existed within Research, Design and Development (RDD), where the quality and speed of innovation depended on Research, Design and Development working seamlessly across disciplines, organisational layers and geographies, particularly the UK and Asia.
data.approach: CorporateDNA partnered with the Group CEO and Executive Committee over an 18+ month journey, including four intensive sessions focused on the team’s Inner Game and Outer Game of Leadership: building trust, constructive challenge, collective accountability and an enterprise mindset. We were subsequently appointed to work within RDD, engaging its senior leadership alongside 75+ Design and Product Managers. Through deep pre-work, candid dialogue and multiple working sessions, we examined how performance, culture and decision-making flowed across Research, Design and Development, surfacing assumptions, difficult hand-offs, process friction and organisational bottlenecks. Leaders then worked together to redefine processes, strengthen alignment and create clearer accountability for how work moved through the system.
data.outcome: At Executive Committee level, the work strengthened the shift from leading individual functions and markets to collectively leading Dyson as an enterprise. Within RDD, engaging 75+ Design and Product Managers took the change beyond the senior team into the layers where products, priorities and decisions actually move. Greater trust and candour enabled issues to surface earlier; clearer processes and hand-offs reduced friction; and stronger alignment created greater empowerment and accountability. Most importantly, leaders strengthened a culture of collective ownership, taking responsibility not simply for their part of the innovation process, but for how the whole system performed.

data.title: Frasers Property
data.headline: Building the next generation of leaders and talent for One Frasers.
data.introduction: A [three]-year partnership strengthening leadership across Frasers Property, from the Group CEO and executive leadership team to successive generations of enterprise talent.
data.challenge: As Frasers Property advanced its One Frasers transformation, the opportunity was to build a stronger enterprise leadership pipeline across markets, functions and leadership generations. This meant going beyond individual capability: creating greater ownership, stronger connections across organisational boundaries and a shared leadership language that could translate the transformation ambition into how leaders showed up every day.
data.approach: CorporateDNA built an integrated, multi-year leadership architecture spanning [three] levels of talent (ELT, Forge and Ignite) across CEO-1, CEO-2 and CEO-3 populations. This was reinforced through Group CEO coaching, executive leadership team development, facilitation and individual coaching. Rather than treating each intervention separately, the work connected leadership generations around the One Frasers transformation narrative, building shared language, behaviours and enterprise-wide capability.
data.outcome: Now in its third year, the partnership has created an alumni community of 100+ senior leaders globally. Leaders are showing greater ownership of the transformation, using a shared language and narrative and demonstrating visible shifts in how they lead. Collaboration is strengthening across markets and functions, with leaders increasingly looking beyond their own market, function or patch to make decisions through an enterprise lens. The result is a transformation that is moving beyond words and becoming visible in everyday leadership behaviour.

data.title: Frasers Property
data.headline: From HR leadership team to enterprise leadership team.
data.introduction: Partnering with Frasers Property’s Group CHRO and People and Culture Leadership Team to build a more aligned, interdependent and enterprise-minded team, equipped to help lead the One Frasers transformation.
data.quote:
This journey helped us step up as an enterprise PCLT: not just as strong individuals, but as a high-performing team that trusts and supports one another.”
Vicki Ng, Group Chief People Officer, Frasers Property Limited
data.challenge: As Frasers Property progressed its One Frasers strategy, the People and Culture Leadership Team needed to evolve alongside it. The opportunity was to move beyond a group of strong functional and market leaders towards a genuinely interdependent enterprise team: one able to think horizontally, challenge constructively, make decisions collectively and influence culture, talent and performance across the organisation. This required not another HR initiative, but a shift in how the team itself operated and led.
data.approach: CorporateDNA designed an 18-month, multi-modal team transformation journey combining immersive team modules, 360° feedback, individual coaching, group coaching, mastery sessions and regular team check-ins. Alongside the leadership work, a series of Action Learning Labs put real Frasers business and organisational challenges into the room, requiring leaders to practise new behaviours while solving live problems together. The journey continually connected the team’s Inner Game (trust, candour, assumptions and leadership behaviour) with its Outer Game of priorities, decisions, collaboration and enterprise impact.
data.outcome: Over 18 months, the PCLT developed stronger trust and connection, greater candour and a clearer sense of collective accountability. Leaders became more willing to surface assumptions, challenge one another constructively and work across geographic and functional boundaries. Decision-making became more collective and the team increasingly shifted from representing individual markets or disciplines to asking “What is right for One Frasers?” The result was a P&C leadership team better able to operate as an enterprise partner in shaping culture, talent, transformation and performance.

data.title: GSK
data.headline: Turning global strategy into local leadership alignment, priorities and behaviour.
data.introduction: Partnering with GSK Mexico to align a new General Manager and local leadership around one culture, shared priorities and new ways of working, and cascade them through the organisation.
data.challenge: GSK Mexico was navigating a significant cultural integration: a new expatriate General Manager, an established local leadership team and the need to translate GSK’s global ambition into something meaningful and actionable in-market. The challenge was not simply to align on values, but to create shared priorities, behaviours and ways of working, and make them real across multiple layers of leadership.
data.approach: CorporateDNA worked first with the GM and leadership team to create alignment around business priorities, values, behaviours and ways of working. We then built a nine-month cascade through LT-1, LT-2 and LT-3, mobilising 70 change agents across the organisation. The journey combined facilitated leadership interventions, group coaching and action learning, with teams translating the ambition into practical action and building quarterly proof points that demonstrated where change was becoming real.
data.outcome: The work moved culture from aspiration into everyday leadership practice. GSK Mexico saw a 30% improvement in decision-making agility and a 71% improvement in climate scores. Leaders developed greater alignment around priorities, clearer ownership and a more consistent way of working across levels. Quarterly proof points made progress visible, helping sustain momentum and demonstrating that culture change was translating into how decisions were made, teams collaborated and the Mexico business operated.

data.bannerStatement: Turn strategic intent into leadership behaviour that changes how the organisation actually operates.

data.title: Ma'aden
data.headline: From an HR leadership team to an enterprise leadership force.
data.introduction: Partnering with Ma’aden’s Group CHRO and HR Leadership Team to strengthen their collective influence, upwards to the Group Executive Committee and horizontally across one of Saudi Arabia’s most important and rapidly growing enterprises.
data.challenge: As Ma’aden grows at extraordinary pace, its HR Leadership Team has a critical role in enabling the organisation to perform and transform. The opportunity was to move beyond a collection of highly capable functional leaders towards a genuinely interdependent enterprise team: able to influence upwards at Group Executive level, work horizontally across organisational boundaries and collectively shape decisions on people, culture, performance and business priorities.
data.approach: CorporateDNA worked with the Group CHRO and HRLT to surface the dynamics that were limiting collective performance: challenging assumptions, breaking through false harmony and creating greater candour around the issues that mattered. Together, the team built a renewed HRLT Charter, clarified collective versus functional accountabilities and established new ways of working. A critical part of the journey was creating a new leadership contract: what the team needed from its leader, what the leader needed from the team, and what members would hold one another accountable for.
data.outcome: The shift was visible in the room and beyond it. Trust strengthened significantly, difficult issues were surfaced earlier and with greater candour, and leaders began moving from representing their individual functions to taking greater ownership for the whole. The renewed charter and leadership contract created clearer mutual accountability and stronger peer-to-peer challenge. The HRLT increasingly operates as a more horizontal, collaborative and interdependent team, better positioned to influence enterprise decisions and enable Ma’aden’s growth agenda.

data.title: Morgan Stanley
data.headline: When technology changes fast, culture has to move with it.
data.introduction: Bringing 200 Morgan Stanley Technology Directors together to turn culture from something discussed into something collectively owned.
data.challenge: At a time of significant change for Morgan Stanley, Technology needed its leaders to do more than respond to transformation; they needed to shape the culture required to deliver it. Sponsored by the Chief Technology Officer in New York, the challenge was to bring 200 Technology Directors into an unusually open conversation about how the function really operated: where ownership was strong, where healthy challenge was being muted, whose voices were heard, and what needed to change for the function to perform at its best.
data.approach: CorporateDNA began with extensive pre-work, including senior stakeholder interviews and a focused assessment of the function’s values, cultural patterns and leadership dynamics. Those insights became the foundation for a highly participative leadership experience: not a presentation about culture, but a space in which leaders could examine it together. We introduced radical candour, healthy challenge, ownership and cognitive diversity, deliberately creating conditions for different perspectives across the 200 directors to be heard rather than allowing hierarchy or dominant voices to shape the conversation. The experience was amplified through sporting metaphors and sporting inspiration, bringing to life lessons about performance, challenge, team contribution and collective responsibility. The Chairman also joined as a guest contributor, connecting the conversation to the wider leadership and organisational context.
data.outcome: The intervention shifted culture from an abstract organisational idea into something leaders could see in their everyday choices, conversations and behaviours. It gave directors permission to challenge more constructively, surface different perspectives and examine the responsibility each leader carried for the culture around them. Most importantly, it reframed culture as something the Technology function didn’t simply inherit from Morgan Stanley, but something 200 influential leaders collectively created every day.

data.title: Vodafone
data.headline: Building a leadership pipeline that lasted well beyond the programme.
data.introduction: For seven consecutive years, Vodafone entrusted CorporateDNA with developing its most promising senior talent, building the enterprise capability, visibility and readiness required for the next generation of global leadership.
data.challenge: Each year, approximately 100 high-potential leaders across Vodafone’s global operating companies were nominated for Inspired. Drawn from CEO-1 and CEO-2 populations, these were already accomplished leaders. The challenge was to prepare them to step beyond functional or market success and operate with the judgement, influence and enterprise perspective required at Vodafone’s most senior levels.
data.approach: CorporateDNA designed and delivered a four-module journey spanning Leading Self, Leading Teams, Leading Peers and Leading the Business. A strong personal-leadership foundation was deliberately connected to the commercial and enterprise demands of senior leadership. Participants worked across markets, functions and cultures, with practical business application embedded throughout. Direct sponsorship from the Group CEO and Group CHRO created exceptional visibility and accountability, positioning Inspired not as another leadership programme, but as an investment in Vodafone’s future leadership bench.
data.outcome: Across seven years, 60 to 70% of participants progressed through promotion, alongside an exceptional Net Promoter Score of 91. Inspired created a global alumni community with broader networks, stronger enterprise perspective and greater readiness for increasingly complex leadership roles. Its longer-term legacy is even more compelling: several alumni have since reached CXO and other senior executive positions within Vodafone, while others have gone on to significant leadership roles across major multinationals around the world.
data.bannerStatement: Build the leadership pipeline before the business needs it.
data.approachHeadline: Seven years. Four dimensions of leadership. One global pipeline.
data.outcomeHeadline: Potential became progression, and progression became legacy.
